sentences.text: Harold Pryce is the person being assessed.
Tom Okafor is a social worker from Harbridge adult services.
Dr Bell requested Tom Okafor to visit Harold Pryce.
The purpose of the visit is to discuss Harold's daily living situation at home.
Sandra is Harold's wife and currently at the shops.
Sandra will be back in about an hour.
Harold has a daughter named Carol who lives in Kestwick, about two hours away.
Carol calls Harold on Sundays.
Harold has a walking stick and a frame upstairs.
Harold had a fall in the garden in the spring.
Harold has not had any falls since the spring.
Harold can wash himself but uses a stool in the shower.
Harold finds socks difficult to manage.
Sandra cooks meals for Harold.
Harold can make a sandwich.
Harold and Sandra have been married for nine years.
Harold's first wife, Joan, died in 2013.
Harold says Sandra manages his medication and keeps it in her handbag.
Harold does not always receive his medication.
Harold did not receive his heart tablets for three days last week.
Harold says he has previously missed heart tablets and water tablets.
Dr Bell observed bruises on Harold's arms.
Harold says he bruises easily due to medication.
Harold says the bruises on his arms were caused by Sandra hitting him with her walking stick when she gets cross.
Harold says Sandra hits him with her walking stick on his arms when she is cross.
Harold says Sandra hits him once a week, or more if she has a bad day.
Harold says Sandra locks him in the bedroom when she goes out.
Harold says Sandra locks him in the bedroom two or three times a week for the afternoon.
Harold says there is no toilet in the bedroom.
Harold says he wants his medication to be delivered to him in blister packs so he can hold them.
